topics.name: B1.1 Cell structures
points: B1.1a Light microscopes, staining and magnification calculations (PAG B1)
B1.1b Sub-cellular structures of eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and their functions
B1.1c How electron microscopy increased understanding of sub-cellular structures

topics.name: B1.2 What happens in cells (and what do cells need)?
points: B1.2a-c DNA as a polymer: double helix, nucleotides and complementary base pairing (DNA extraction, PAG B2)
B1.2d-e Protein synthesis and how DNA base sequence (triplet code) determines the protein
B1.2f-g Enzymes: active site, specificity, factors affecting activity and investigating enzyme-controlled reactions (PAG B4)

topics.name: B1.3 Respiration
points: B1.3a-b Cellular respiration as a universal, exothermic process supplying ATP
B1.3c Aerobic and anaerobic respiration in plants, fungi and animals
B1.3d-f Synthesis and breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids (food tests, PAG B2)

topics.name: B1.4 Photosynthesis
points: B1.4a-c Photosynthetic organisms as producers; the process of photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction
B1.4d Experiments showing light is needed for photosynthesis (starch test, PAG B5)
B1.4e-f Effects of temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide on rate; limiting factors (PAG B5)

topics.name: B2.1 Supplying the cell
points: B2.1a Diffusion, osmosis and active transport (osmosis practical, PAG B8)
B2.1b Mitosis and the cell cycle (root tip squash, PAG B1)
B2.1c Cell differentiation and specialised cells
B2.1d-f Stem cells in animals and meristems in plants; embryonic and adult stem cells

topics.name: B2.2 The challenges of size
points: B2.2a-b Surface area to volume ratio and the need for exchange surfaces and transport systems
B2.2c Human circulatory system: double circulation
B2.2d Structure and function of the heart and blood vessels
B2.2e Red blood cells and plasma adapted for transport
B2.2f Root hair cells and uptake of water and mineral ions
B2.2g-h Transpiration, translocation, stomata, xylem and phloem
B2.2i-j Factors affecting rate of water uptake; using a potometer (PAG B8)

topics.name: B3.1 Coordination and control: the nervous system
points: B3.1a-b Structure of the nervous system, neurones and coordinated responses
B3.1c Reflex arcs (reaction time practical, PAG B6)
B3.1d-e Structure and function of the eye; eye defects and their treatment
B3.1f-h The brain: regions, investigating brain function and limits of treating damage

topics.name: B3.2 Coordination and control: the endocrine system
points: B3.2a-b Principles of hormonal control; thyroxine, adrenaline and negative feedback
B3.2c-d Hormones in reproduction: the menstrual cycle, FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone
B3.2e Hormonal and non-hormonal methods of contraception
B3.2f Hormones in reproductive technologies to treat infertility
B3.2g Auxins in phototropism and gravitropism (PAG B6)
B3.2h-i Effects and uses of plant hormones: auxins, gibberellins and ethene

topics.name: B3.3 Maintaining internal environments
points: B3.3a Importance of maintaining a constant internal environment
B3.3b Thermoregulation and the role of the skin
B3.3c-d Control of blood glucose by insulin and glucagon
B3.3e Type 1 and type 2 diabetes and their treatment
B3.3f Effects of osmotic changes on cells
B3.3g-h The kidneys: role in water balance, gross structure and kidney tubules
B3.3i ADH and negative feedback in controlling water balance
B3.3j Responses to temperature and osmotic challenges

topics.name: B7 Practical skills (assessed in all papers)
points: PAG B1 Microscopy
PAG B2 Testing for biological molecules
PAG B3 Sampling techniques
PAG B4 Rates of enzyme-controlled reactions
PAG B5 Photosynthesis
PAG B6 Physiology, responses and respiration
PAG B7 Microbiological techniques
PAG B8 Transport in and out of cells

topics.name: B4.1 Ecosystems
points: B4.1a-b Cycling of materials (carbon, nitrogen) and the role of decomposers
B4.1c Importance of the carbon and water cycles
B4.1d Effect of temperature, water and oxygen on decomposition rate
B4.1e Levels of organisation within an ecosystem
B4.1f Abiotic and biotic factors affecting communities (PAG B3)
B4.1g Interdependence and competition: predation, mutualism and parasitism
B4.1h Trophic levels: producers and consumers
B4.1i-j Pyramids of biomass and efficiency of biomass transfer between trophic levels

topics.name: B5.1 Inheritance
points: B5.1a-b Key genetic terms: allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype, phenotype; the genome
B5.1c Genome and environment determine phenotype; discontinuous and continuous variation
B5.1d-e Mutations and genetic variants in coding and non-coding DNA
B5.1f Advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction
B5.1g-h Haploid and diploid; meiosis and genetic variation
B5.1i-j Single gene inheritance and Punnett squares
B5.1k Sex determination in humans
B5.1l Most phenotypic features result from multiple genes
B5.1m Development of understanding of genetics, including Mendel's work

topics.name: B5.2 Natural selection and evolution
points: B5.2a Genetic variation in populations
B5.2b Impact of developments in biology on classification systems
B5.2c-d Natural selection and evolution, including formation of new species
B5.2e Evidence for evolution: fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria
B5.2f Development of the theory of natural selection by Darwin and Wallace

topics.name: B6.1 Monitoring and maintaining the environment
points: B6.1a Investigating distribution and abundance of organisms using sampling (PAG B3)
B6.1b Human interactions with ecosystems and their effects on biodiversity
B6.1c Benefits and challenges of maintaining local and global biodiversity
B6.1d Evaluating evidence for environmental change affecting distribution of organisms

topics.name: B6.2 Feeding the human race
points: B6.2a Biological factors affecting food security
B6.2b Agricultural solutions to the demands of a growing population
B6.2c Selective breeding of food plants and domesticated animals
B6.2d-e Genetic engineering: principles and main steps
B6.2f Benefits and risks of gene technology in agriculture
B6.2g Biotechnology, including GM, to meet the demands of the growing population

topics.name: B6.3 Monitoring and maintaining health
points: B6.3a-c Health and disease; communicable and non-communicable diseases; interactions between diseases
B6.3d-f Spread of communicable diseases in animals and plants, prevention, and examples of infections
B6.3g-i Plant defences against disease; detecting and identifying plant diseases
B6.3j-l Human defences: white blood cells, platelets, non-specific defences and the immune system
B6.3m-n Monoclonal antibodies: production and uses
B6.3o Vaccines and medicines in preventing and treating disease
B6.3p Aseptic techniques for culturing microorganisms (PAG B7)
B6.3q Discovery and development of new medicines
B6.3r-t Non-communicable diseases: risk factors, lifestyle and treating cardiovascular disease
B6.3u Cancer as uncontrolled cell growth
B6.3v Benefits and risks of using stem cells in medicine
B6.3w-x Gene technology in medicine and using the human genome to predict disease and target treatments
